docs.title: Under the hood
docs.text:
graph LR
    UI["React app"] --> API["FastAPI backend"]
    MCP["Claude via MCP"] --> API
    API --> DB[("Neo4j<br/>knowledge graph")]
    API --> Drive["Google Drive<br/>PDFs and figures"]
    API --> LLM["Claude / any<br/>OpenAI-compatible model"]
    API --> Ext["Semantic Scholar<br/>CrossRef · arXiv"]

Every paper, author, topic, project, note and concept is a node in one Neo4j graph, so the same data powers the library, the chat, the concept map and the Cypher editor. PDFs stay in your own Google Drive. More in Architecture.

PaperManager is open source. The project page at niklas-abraham.de has the story behind it; issues and pull requests are welcome on GitHub.

docs.title: DB: Neo4j Aura (cloud) over SQLite
docs.text: Papers, people, topics, and tags are naturally a graph. Enables path queries, co-authorship derivation, topic clustering. Free tier (200k nodes / 400k relationships) sufficient for personal use.

docs.title: Tags as nodes, not property arrays
docs.text: Tags are first-class citizens for filtering and browsing. (Paper)-[:TAGGED]->(Tag) lets you query "all papers with this tag" efficiently.

docs.title: Topic ≠ Tag
docs.text:
• Topic = formal research area, linked to Person specialties
  • Tag = free-form personal label (source, status, context, anything)

docs.title: Notes as separate nodes
docs.text: Notes need their own @mention and #topic relationships. A text field on Paper would lose this graph power.

docs.title: INVOLVES relationship with role property
docs.text: Instead of many typed relationships for workflow states, one INVOLVES {role} relationship keeps the schema flexible. New roles can be invented freely without schema changes.

docs.title: Metadata extraction: four-layer chain
docs.text:
1. DOI regex → Semantic Scholar API (preferred) or CrossRef (fallback) — covers ~80–90% of papers
  2. Ollama + llama3.2:3b local LLM — for papers without DOI (drafts, internal reports)
  3. Regex heuristics — last resort, user corrects in UI
  4. Abstract fallback: ABSTRACT_RE regex → Claude Haiku

metadata_source field on Paper node records which layer was used. Semantic Scholar also returns topics + citation count → auto-populates Topic nodes.

docs.title: MCP server shares the same service layer as FastAPI
docs.text: db/queries/ and services/ are framework-neutral. FastAPI routers/ and MCP tools/ are two thin entry-point layers over the same logic. Every capability is available both via HTTP and via Claude Desktop tool calls. PDF upload is intentionally not exposed as an MCP tool — file upload via browser only.

docs.title: No Collection node (for now)
docs.text: Projects serve a similar purpose and are already in scope. Can revisit if the need for lightweight grouping (reading lists) emerges.

docs.title: Backend: FastAPI
docs.text: Python-native, strong async support, automatic OpenAPI docs.

docs.title: Frontend: React + Vite + Tailwind
docs.text: Standard modern SPA stack; fast HMR during development.

docs.title: Knowledge Chat: agentic tool-use over hybrid retrieval
docs.text: Instead of stuffing all paper text into context, the backend pre-loads a relevance-ranked subset and gives Claude two tools: run_cypher (live graph queries) and semantic_search (vector similarity). Claude decides what additional data it needs. This keeps context manageable while allowing Claude to chase any lead in the graph.

docs.title: Vector embeddings on Paper nodes
docs.text: 768-dim Ollama nomic-embed-text embeddings stored directly on Paper.embedding. A Neo4j vector index (paper_embeddings) enables ANN cosine search at query time. Chosen over a separate vector store (Pinecone, etc.) to keep the stack minimal.

docs.title: Hybrid retrieval: vector + recency fallback
docs.text: Vector search alone fails when embeddings haven't been generated yet (cold start). The recency fallback (10 most recently added papers) ensures Knowledge Chat is useful from day one without a backfill step.

docs.title: Conversation compaction with structured working memory
docs.text: Simple truncation loses context. Claude Haiku extracts a JSON block of key findings, open questions, and decisions before compaction. Specific numbers and paper titles survive in the structured JSON even after the messages are replaced.

docs.title: Claims as graph nodes
docs.text: Claim extraction enables evidence-level queries via Cypher. Claims are NOT injected into Knowledge Chat context by default (would bloat it); Claude pulls them on demand via run_cypher when it needs evidence-level detail.

docs.title: Chapters for books and lecture decks
docs.text: document_type on Paper controls the upload pipeline. Books and lecture decks skip summary/figures/references/claims but support chapters. Chapters are detected in three passes: Docling structural → regex → Ollama AI.

docs.title: Blogs as first-class nodes
docs.text: Technical blog posts (Distill, Lil'Log, etc.) are valuable context alongside papers. Blog (feed) and BlogPost (individual post) nodes allow the same tag/project/chat workflows used for papers to apply to blog content.

docs.title: Annotations (PDF highlights) stored in Neo4j
docs.text: Highlights stored as Annotation nodes linked to Paper, not as PDF metadata. This keeps annotations queryable and database-portable.

docs.title: Author tracking with Semantic Scholar
docs.text: Person.tracked = true + Person.s2_author_id enables automatic import of new papers. S2 is queried periodically; new papers are ingested just like URL ingest.

docs.title: JWT authentication with admin-managed users
docs.text: Single-user primary focus, but multi-user support needed for collaboration. JWT stored in localStorage; admin user manages create/update/delete. Admin capabilities restricted to username niklas in current implementation.

docs.title: Rate limiting as in-process middleware
docs.text: Sliding-window rate limiter in services/rate_limit.py (no Redis dependency). Stricter limits on /auth/login to prevent brute-force attacks.

docs.title: Docker Compose + Traefik for production
docs.text: Three services: Neo4j, FastAPI backend, Nginx-served React frontend. Traefik handles SSL (Let's Encrypt) and routing. Neo4j and backend are internal-only; only the Nginx container is internet-facing.

docs.title: Hosting your own PaperManager
docs.text:
This guide sets up your own instance with your own database and your own keys. You can run it on your own computer (localhost) or on Heroku. Both use the same container image, Dockerfile.selfhost. It holds the React frontend, served by nginx, and the FastAPI backend, and serves both from one port. The login cookie only works when the page and the API come from the same origin, so they share that port.

docker-compose.example.yml mirrors the maintainer's production stack (Traefik, his domain, a remote GPU machine). Don't use it. Use docker-compose.selfhost.yml or heroku.yml.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
Thing Required? Used for Git and Docker (Docker Desktop on macOS/Windows) yes building and running the app A Google account plus a Google Cloud project yes PDFs are stored in your Google Drive; uploading fails without it An Anthropic API key (console.anthropic.com) strongly recommended summaries, paper chat, Knowledge Chat, topic suggestions An OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g. OpenRouter) optional the "Gemma (LiteLLM)" model option, claim extraction A Heroku account plus the Heroku CLI only for Heroku hosting A Neo4j AuraDB Free instance (console.neo4j.io) only for Heroku the database (locally, Docker runs Neo4j for you)

Expect around 2 GB of RAM for the app container. The PDF layout model (Docling) runs inside it and loads PyTorch.

docs.title: Step 1: get the code and create .env
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/NiklasAbraham/PaperManager.git
cd PaperManager
cp .env.example .env

Edit .env. Keep it private, since it is your secrets file and is git-ignored. Change these values and leave everything else at its default:

NEO4J_PASSWORD=<any long random string>        # locally: Docker creates the DB with this password
JWT_SECRET_KEY=<output of: openssl rand -hex 32>
DEFAULT_USER_NAME=<your login name>             # the owner/admin account
DEFAULT_USER_PASSWORD=                          # leave empty; you set it in step 4
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID=<from step 2>

# The maintainer's private infrastructure: switch it off
DOCLING_MODE=local
INFERENCE_MANAGER_URL=
HERMIONE_HOST=
LITELLM_ENDPOINT=
LITELLM_EMBED_MODEL=

For the optional Gemma model, point LiteLLM at any OpenAI-compatible API, for example LITELLM_ENDPOINT=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, LITELLM_API_KEY=<openrouter key>, LITELLM_MODEL=google/gemma-3-27b-it.

Leave CLAUDE_CODE_USERS and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN empty. That feature runs chats on the server owner's personal Claude subscription, and only the owner may use it. If you have your own Claude Pro/Max plan and want it for yourself, set CLAUDE_CODE_USERS=<your login name>. Then put the output of claude setup-token (from Claude Code) into CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. Never list other people there.

docs.title: Step 2: Google Drive access (once, on your own computer)
docs.text:
1. Go to console.cloud.google.com and create a project. Open APIs & Services → Library, then enable the Google Drive API.
  2. Open APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen. Choose user type External, fill in the app name and your e-mail, and add yourself as a test user.
  3. Open APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID, with application type Desktop app. Download the JSON and save it as backend/credentials.json.
  4. In Google Drive, create a folder for the PDFs. Its ID is the last part of the folder URL (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/<THIS>). Put it into GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID.
  5. Create the login token. A browser window opens; log in and allow access:
python3 -m venv .venv-drive
.venv-drive/bin/pip install google-auth-oauthlib google-api-python-client
.venv-drive/bin/python backend/scripts/setup_drive_oauth.py

This writes backend/token.json. Both credentials.json and token.json are git-ignored. Never commit them.

docs.title: Step 3a: run on localhost
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml up -d --build   # first build takes ~10 min
docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml logs -f app      # wait for "Application startup complete"

Create your account (step 4), then open http://localhost:8080.

  • Stop: docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml down. Your data stays in the neo4j_data volume. down -v deletes it.
  • Update: git pull, then run the up -d --build command again.

docs.title: Step 3b: run on Heroku
docs.text:
Heroku has no free tier and no persistent disk, so the database lives on Neo4j AuraDB Free.

  1. Create an AuraDB Free instance at console.neo4j.io. Save the generated password. Note the connection URI (neo4j+s://xxxx.databases.neo4j.io).
  2. Create the app and switch it to container builds:
heroku login
heroku create <app-name>                  # e.g. papers-alex → https://papers-alex-xxxx.herokuapp.com
heroku stack:set container -a <app-name>
  1. Set the configuration. Use the same values as in .env, plus the Heroku-specific ones:
APP_HOST=<app-name>-xxxx.herokuapp.com    # the host from `heroku apps:info -a <app-name>`
heroku config:set -a <app-name> \
  NEO4J_URI='neo4j+s://xxxx.databases.neo4j.io' NEO4J_USER=neo4j NEO4J_PASSWORD='<aura password>' \
  JWT_SECRET_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)" DEFAULT_USER_NAME='<your login name>' \
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY='sk-ant-...' \
  GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID='<folder id>' \
  GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID='<client_id from credentials.json>' \
  GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET='<client_secret from credentials.json>' \
  GOOGLE_TOKEN_JSON="$(cat backend/token.json)" \
  DOCLING_MODE=local INFERENCE_MANAGER_URL= HERMIONE_HOST= LITELLM_ENDPOINT= LITELLM_EMBED_MODEL= \
  FRONTEND_URL="https://$APP_HOST" TRUSTED_HOSTS="$APP_HOST" TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true

Heroku has no disk to keep token.json on, so GOOGLE_TOKEN_JSON passes its contents as a variable. GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET are inside backend/credentials.json.

  1. Deploy. heroku.yml makes Heroku build Dockerfile.selfhost:
git push heroku main
heroku ps:type web=standard-2x -a <app-name>   # 1 GB RAM; basic (512 MB) runs out of memory
heroku logs --tail -a <app-name>               # wait for "Application startup complete"

If a PDF upload crashes with "Memory quota exceeded" in the logs, the layout model needs more memory. Use performance-m. Heroku also cuts every request off after 30 seconds (error H12). Long PDFs can take longer than that to process, so very large uploads may fail on Heroku even though they work locally.

  1. Create your account (step 4), then open https://<APP_HOST>.

To update: git pull from GitHub, then git push heroku main again.

docs.title: Step 4: create your account
docs.text:
The account named DEFAULT_USER_NAME is the owner and admin. It is also the only account that uses the server-wide ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Other users you add later enter their own key under Settings.

# localhost
docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml exec app python scripts/create_default_user.py
# Heroku
heroku run -a <app-name> python scripts/create_default_user.py

The script asks for a password (at least 8 characters).

Log in, then follow First steps to add your first paper and try the tour, the concept map and the chat.

docs.text: Symptom Cause / fix 400 Invalid host header TRUSTED_HOSTS must list the exact host name you open in the browser Login works but every page says "Session expired" The page and the API are on different origins. docs.title: AI Pipelines
docs.text: PaperManager uses multiple AI models for different tasks. This page documents each pipeline, the models used, and how they fit together.

docs.title: Models Used
docs.text:
Model Provider Used for claude-opus-4-6 Anthropic Paper summarisation, single-paper chat, knowledge chat, cross-paper synthesis, research gap analysis claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 Anthropic Abstract extraction, reference extraction, topic suggestion, claim extraction, chapter summarisation, conversation compaction, figure captioning (claude-vision mode) llama3.2:3b Ollama (local) Metadata extraction (layer 2), tag suggestion, chapter detection, figure captions (default), affiliation extraction, Cypher assist, merge scan nomic-embed-text Ollama (local) Paper embedding vectors for semantic similarity search

All Anthropic calls can be routed through an enterprise Foundry gateway by setting ANTHROPIC_WORK_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_WORK_BASE_URL.

docs.title: Metadata Extraction Pipeline (PDF Upload)
docs.text:
Runs when a PDF is uploaded. Tries strategies in order, stopping at the first success:

flowchart TD
    Start["PDF bytes"] --> Extract["Docling extracts raw_text"]
    Extract --> FindDOI{DOI / arXiv ID\nfound in text?}

    FindDOI -->|"Yes"| S2["Layer 1a: Semantic Scholar API"]
    S2 -->|fail| CR["Layer 1a fallback: CrossRef API"]

    FindDOI -->|"No DOI but\ntitle found"| S2Title["Layer 1b: S2 title search"]

    FindDOI -->|"Nothing found"| Ollama["Layer 2: Ollama llama3.2:3b\non first 3 000 chars"]
    Ollama -->|"Ollama unavailable"| Heuristic["Layer 3: Regex heuristics\n(first line = title, year regex)"]

    S2 --> AbstractCheck{Abstract\nextracted?}
    CR --> AbstractCheck
    S2Title --> AbstractCheck
    Ollama --> AbstractCheck
    Heuristic --> AbstractCheck

    AbstractCheck -->|"No"| AbstractFallback["ABSTRACT_RE regex\n→ Claude Haiku if regex fails"]
    AbstractCheck -->|"Yes"| Done["Metadata ready"]
    AbstractFallback --> Done
Layer Trigger Service Output 1a (primary) DOI or arXiv ID in text Semantic Scholar API title, year, authors, abstract, topics, citation count, venue 1a (fallback) S2 fails CrossRef API title, year, authors, doi, venue 1b Title found, no DOI S2 title search same as 1a 2 No DOI, no useful title Ollama llama3.2:3b on raw_text[:3000] title, year, authors (structured JSON) 3 Ollama unavailable Regex on raw_text title (first non-empty line), year (4-digit year regex) Abstract fallback Abstract still missing ABSTRACT_RE regex → Claude Haiku abstract text

The metadata_source property on the Paper node records which layer was used.

docs.title: Paper Summarisation
docs.text:
Triggered after PDF upload or via POST /backfill/summary / POST /{id}/regenerate-summary.

flowchart LR
    A["abstract + raw_text"] --> P["Load prompts/summary.txt"]
    P --> C["Claude Opus 4.6"]
    C --> S["summary string\nsaved to Paper.summary"]

The prompt at prompts/summary.txt structures output as: Problem / motivation · Key method or contribution · Main findings · Relevance.

docs.title: Topic Suggestion
docs.text:
Triggered during upload, via POST /papers/{id}/topics/suggest, or bulk backfill.

flowchart LR
    A["title + abstract"] --> P["Load prompts/topics.txt"]
    P --> C["Claude Haiku"]
    C --> T["3–6 title-case topic strings"]
    T --> DB["MERGE Topic nodes\n+ ABOUT relationships"]

docs.title: Tag Suggestion
docs.text:
Triggered in the upload modal (optional step) or via POST /tags/suggest.

flowchart LR
    A["title + abstract"] --> O["Ollama llama3.2:3b"]
    O --> Tags["List of tag names\nfrom seeded tag vocabulary"]

docs.title: Reference Extraction Pipeline
docs.text:
Triggered via GET /papers/{id}/extract-references or POST /papers/{id}/references.

flowchart TD
    Start["Paper with raw_text"] --> A{DOI available?}
    A -->|"Yes"| S2["Strategy A:\nSemantic Scholar /references API"]
    A -->|"No"| B["Strategy B:\nRegex on REFERENCES section"]
    S2 -->|"< 3 results"| B
    B -->|"< 3 results"| Claude["Strategy C:\nClaude Haiku on last 30%\nof raw_text"]
    S2 -->|"≥ 3 results"| Done["Reference list"]
    B -->|"≥ 3 results"| Done
    Claude --> Done

Each reference creates a Paper stub node tagged from-references and linked via CITES. Stubs are enriched when the full paper is later imported.

docs.title: Claim Extraction
docs.text:
Triggered automatically during upload (for papers) or via POST /papers/{id}/claims/extract.

flowchart LR
    A["raw_text + title"] --> P["Load prompts/claims.txt"]
    P --> C["Claude Haiku"]
    C --> Claims["List of {text, type} claims"]
    Claims --> DB["Create Claim nodes\nHAS_CLAIM relationships"]

Claim types include "finding", "method", "limitation", "contribution".

docs.title: Paper Embedding
docs.text:
Triggered during upload (if enabled in settings) or via backfill.

flowchart LR
    A["title + abstract"] --> O["Ollama nomic-embed-text"]
    O --> V["768-dim embedding vector"]
    V --> DB["Stored on Paper.embedding\n(vector index for ANN search)"]

docs.title: Single-Paper Chat
docs.text:
Triggered via POST /papers/{id}/chat.

The model is selected per-request: Claude Opus (default), Claude Work (enterprise gateway), or Ollama.

docs.title: Chapter Detection (Books / Lecture Decks)
docs.text:
Triggered via POST /papers/{id}/chapters/detect.

flowchart TD
    PDF["PDF from Google Drive"] --> Docling["Strategy 1: Docling\nstructural chapter detection"]
    Docling -->|"found chapters"| Done["Create Chapter nodes"]
    Docling -->|"no chapters"| Regex["Strategy 2: Regex\non raw_text headings"]
    Regex -->|"found chapters"| Done
    Regex -->|"no chapters"| AI["Strategy 3: Ollama AI\n(use_ai=true only)"]
    AI --> Done
    Done --> Summarize["Ollama summarizes\neach chapter"]

Each chapter node stores its text slice, title, level, page range, and summary.

Chapter chat uses prompts/chapter_chat_system.txt with Claude Haiku; chapter summary uses prompts/chapter_summary.txt with Ollama.

docs.title: Figure Extraction & Captioning
docs.text:
Triggered via POST /papers/{id}/figures/extract.

flowchart TD
    PDF["PDF from Google Drive"] --> Docling["Docling: extract\npage images + figure regions"]
    Docling --> Method{Caption method\nfrom settings}
    Method -->|"docling"| DocCaption["Docling structural caption"]
    Method -->|"ollama"| OllamaCaption["Ollama llama3.2:3b\nfrom prompts/figure_captions.txt"]
    Method -->|"claude-vision"| ClaudeCaption["Claude Haiku Vision"]
    DocCaption --> Upload["Upload PNG to Google Drive"]
    OllamaCaption --> Upload
    ClaudeCaption --> Upload
    Upload --> DB["Save Figure node in Neo4j"]

docs.title: Figure Vision Chat
docs.text: Triggered via POST /papers/{id}/figures/{fig_id}/chat. The figure image is retrieved from Google Drive and sent to Claude with the question.

docs.title: Cross-Paper Synthesis
docs.text:
Triggered via POST /synthesis.

flowchart LR
    Q["paper_ids + question"] --> Papers["Fetch Paper nodes"]
    Papers --> P["Load prompts/synthesis.txt"]
    P --> C["Claude Opus\n(+ optional web search)"]
    C --> R["Synthesis text"]

docs.title: Research Gap Analysis
docs.text:
Triggered via POST /research-gaps.

flowchart LR
    Q["topic + paper_ids / project_id"] --> Papers["Fetch relevant papers"]
    Papers --> P["Load prompts/research_gaps.txt"]
    P --> C["Claude Opus\n(+ optional web search)"]
    C --> R["Gap analysis text"]

docs.title: Knowledge Chat Context Assembly
docs.text:
Triggered via POST /knowledge-chat/stream.

flowchart TD
    Q["User question"] --> Parse["Parse @mentions\n@tag:, @topic:, @project:, @paper:"]
    Parse -->|"Mentions found"| Cypher["Run Cypher queries\nto fetch matching papers"]
    Parse -->|"No mentions"| Recent["Fetch 10 most recently\nadded papers"]
    Cypher --> Budget["Apply token budget\nper paper (truncate raw_text)"]
    Recent --> Budget
    Budget --> System["Load prompts/knowledge_chat_system.txt"]
    System --> Claude["Claude Opus 4.6\n(streaming SSE)"]
    Claude --> Browser["Token-by-token response"]

docs.title: Affiliation Extraction
docs.text:
Triggered as part of paper upload when author affiliations are missing.

flowchart LR
    T["raw_text first 2 000 chars"] --> P["Load prompts/author_affiliations.txt"]
    P --> O["Ollama llama3.2:3b"]
    O --> A["author → affiliation mapping"]
    A --> DB["Update Person.affiliation in Neo4j"]

docs.title: Duplicate Detection (Merge Scan)
docs.text:
Triggered via POST /merge/scan.

flowchart LR
    A["All papers (title + doi)"] --> Pairs["Find candidate pairs\nby string similarity"]
    Pairs --> P["Load prompts/merge_scan.txt"]
    P --> C["Ollama or Claude\n(batches of 30 pairs)"]
    C --> Results["Scored duplicate pairs\n(similarity 0–1 + reason)"]

docs.title: Literature Search Keywords
docs.text:
Triggered via POST /literature/search.

The keyword list in prompts/literature_search_keywords.txt (or a project's stored keywords) is used to query arXiv, PubMed, and bioRxiv. Results are streamed via SSE and marked as already-in-library where applicable.

docs.title: The Shared Layer Principle
docs.text:
The most important architectural rule in PaperManager:

db/queries/ and services/ are framework-neutral. Neither FastAPI nor MCP specifics leak into them. routers/ and tools/ are two different entry points over the same logic.

This means every capability is available both via HTTP (for the browser) and via MCP tool calls (for Claude Desktop), without any code duplication.

docs.title: Paper Ingestion Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Browser
    participant Router as routers/papers.py
    participant PDFParser as services/pdf_parser.py
    participant MetaLookup as services/metadata_lookup.py
    participant Drive as services/drive.py
    participant AI as services/ai.py
    participant DB as db/queries/papers.py
    participant Neo4j

    Browser->>Router: POST /papers/upload (PDF bytes)
    Router->>PDFParser: extract_text(pdf_bytes)
    PDFParser-->>Router: raw_text
    Router->>PDFParser: find_doi(raw_text)
    alt DOI found
        Router->>MetaLookup: lookup_semantic_scholar(doi)
        alt S2 fails
            Router->>MetaLookup: lookup_crossref(doi)
        end
    else No DOI
        Router->>PDFParser: extract_metadata_with_llm(raw_text[:3000])
        alt Ollama unavailable
            Router->>PDFParser: extract_metadata_heuristic(raw_text)
        end
    end
    Router->>Drive: upload_pdf(pdf_bytes)
    Drive-->>Router: drive_file_id
    Router->>AI: summarize_paper(abstract, raw_text)
    AI-->>Router: summary
    Router->>AI: extract_claims(raw_text)
    AI-->>Router: claims
    Router->>DB: create_paper(metadata + summary + drive_file_id)
    DB->>Neo4j: MERGE (p:Paper {...})

See ingestion-workflow.md for the full staged workflow including the parse/confirm/upload/onboarding flow.

docs.title: Key Design Decisions
docs.text:
See the full Decisions Log for rationale. The key principles:

  1. Neo4j over SQL — papers, people, topics, and tags are naturally a graph
  2. Tags as nodes — (Paper)-[:TAGGED]->(Tag) allows efficient "all papers with tag X" queries
  3. Topic ≠ Tag — Topics are formal research areas; Tags are free-form personal labels
  4. Notes as graph nodes — Notes have their own @mention and #topic relationships
  5. Shared service layer — MCP tools and HTTP routers call the same db/ and services/ code
  6. Prompts as files — All prompt templates live in prompts/ and are loaded fresh on each call
  7. Vector embeddings — Paper nodes store Ollama embeddings for semantic similarity search
  8. User identity — User nodes enable per-user conversation history and attribution

docs.title: main.py — App Entry Point
docs.text:
main.py creates the FastAPI application, sets up CORS, registers all routers, and defines a startup lifespan:

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    get_driver().verify_connectivity()   # verify Neo4j
    run_schema_setup(get_driver())       # create indexes + constraints
    seed_default_tags(get_driver())      # seed default tags
    seed_people_tags(get_driver())       # seed people-related tags
    yield

docs.title: Ingestion Workflow
docs.text: How papers enter the library, what runs when, and why.

docs.title: Stage 1 — Parse + preprocess + preanalyze (immediate, on drop)
docs.text:
Three requests start as soon as you drop a file. Nothing is saved.

1a — Metadata (POST /papers/parse)

Step What runs Cost Extract raw text pypdf local, fast Find DOI / arXiv ID regex on first page local, fast Metadata lookup Semantic Scholar → CrossRef API network LiteLLM fallback first 3 000 chars local, ~2 s Heuristics fallback first-line title, year regex local, instant Abstract extraction regex → Claude Haiku if needed conditional

1b — Layout (POST /papers/preprocess)

Step What runs Cost Docling figures + tables (once per PDF hash) GPU / slow

1c — Analysis (POST /papers/preanalyze) — the heavy LLM work, precomputed

Step What runs Cost summary summarize_paper (default instructions) LLM ai_topics suggest_topics LLM claims extract_claims LLM references extract_references LLM / network affiliations extract_affiliations_with_litellm LLM tag_suggestions suggest_tags_litellm LLM

Result: metadata pre-fills the modal; figures/tables and the full LLM analysis are cached on disk (keyed by PDF SHA-256). No paper is created.

The queue row turns green ("Ready — click to review") only once metadata, layout, and analysis are all ready — meaning Upload will be a pure save with no LLM work. The queue is persisted to IndexedDB and re-verified on return.

Normative spec: .specs/009_upload_queue_workflow.md

docs.title: Stage 2 — Confirm (modal, user-driven)
docs.text:
You open the modal, verify the pre-filled metadata, and pick the document type. Document type controls what runs in Stage 3:

Type Summary Figures References Paper (default) ✓ ✓ ✓ Book ✗ ✗ ✗ Lecture deck ✗ ✗ ✗

Nothing is saved until you click Upload →.

docs.title: Stage 3 — Upload (triggered on confirm)
docs.text:
Triggered by: POST /papers/upload Runs synchronously — the modal spinner shows while this completes.

PDF bytes
  │
  ├─ 0. load cached analysis      → analysis_key → result.json (no LLM)
  │
  ├─ 1. metadata                  → REUSE cached meta (else extract_metadata)
  │
  ├─ 2. title_override            → apply any title edit from the modal
  │
  ├─ 3. Drive upload              → stores PDF, returns drive_file_id
  │
  ├─ 4. summary                   → REUSE cached summary                     [PAPER only]
  │       re-runs summarize_paper ONLY if you edited the instructions
  │
  ├─ 5. embed_paper               → skipped unless litellm_embed_model is set
  │
  ├─ 6. save to Neo4j             → Paper node created (or stub enriched)
  │       duplicate check: 409 if paper with drive_file_id already exists
  │
  ├─ 7. link authors              → Person nodes, REUSE cached affiliations, S2 IDs
  │       7b. enrichment          → ORCID + S2 HTTP (not LLM, 24h cooldown)
  │
  ├─ 8. link topics              → Semantic Scholar topics + REUSE cached AI topics
  │
  ├─ 9. claims                   → REUSE cached claims                       [PAPER only]
  │
  ├─ 10. references              → REUSE cached references                   [PAPER only]
  │
  └─ 12. figures + tables        → reuse Stage 1b cache; upload images to Drive  [PAPER only]

With a fully-precomputed (green) row, Upload makes no LLM calls — everything is reused from the analysis cache. The only intentional LLM call is the summary, and only if you edited the summary instructions in the modal.

Where the Upload time goes: ~1–2 s Drive PDF upload + Neo4j writes + ORCID/S2 enrichment, then ~10–15 s uploading figure/table images to Google Drive (step 12). That last step is the bulk of the wait and is not precomputed by design.

Docling runs at most once per PDF: during Stage 1b (queue) when possible; upload step 12 only runs Docling if preprocess failed or was skipped.

docs.title: Stage 4 — Onboarding (modal, user-driven)
docs.text:
After the upload completes the modal walks through:

  1. References — review extracted references, uncheck any to skip
  2. Tags — AI-suggested + your existing tags, add custom ones
  3. Project — optionally assign to a project
  4. People — link supervisor / colleague / who shared it

These steps are purely interactive and make no AI calls.

docs.title: Why extract_metadata runs twice
docs.text:
Stage 1 (/papers/parse) extracts metadata to pre-fill the modal. Stage 3 (/papers/upload) needs to re-run it because the raw text is required for the summary and is too large to pass through the frontend. The Stage 1 result is discarded client-side after filling the form.

Consequence: Ollama + S2 API calls happen twice per paper. Summary and figures happen once.

docs.title: URL Ingest
docs.text:
Triggered by: POST /papers/from-url-full

URL
  │
  ├─ resolve metadata (arXiv API / S2 / CrossRef / PubMed)
  │
  ├─ download PDF (arXiv / bioRxiv only — others blocked by Cloudflare)
  │
  ├─ [if PDF available]
  │     ├─ extract_metadata from PDF
  │     ├─ Drive upload
  │     ├─ summarize_paper (full text)
  │     ├─ save to Neo4j
  │     ├─ extract references
  │     └─ extract figures
  │
  └─ [if no PDF]
        ├─ summarize_paper (abstract only — shorter, weaker)
        └─ save to Neo4j (no drive_file_id, no raw_text)

Modal still shows refs → tags → project → people onboarding after this completes.

docs.title: Duplicate handling
docs.text:
Scenario Outcome Same DOI / title in queue, not yet uploaded Both show "Ready". First to upload wins; second gets 409 in the modal. Paper already in library (has PDF) Caught in Stage 1 duplicate check → queue row shows "Already in your library" Paper exists as a stub (URL-ingested, no PDF) Upload enriches the stub with full text, new summary, figures. Old abstract-based summary is replaced.

The stub enrichment case is the only scenario where a summary is regenerated — and it's intentional: the full-text summary from Stage 3 is better than the abstract-only summary from URL ingest.

docs.title: Book / Lecture Deck
docs.text:
When you select Book or Lecture Deck in the modal:

  • Steps 4, 9, 10, 11 (summary, claims, references, figures) are all skipped
  • Tags book or lecture_deck are applied automatically
  • Chapter structure can be detected afterwards via Chapters tab on the paper detail page

docs.title: Manual operations (on-demand, never automatic)
docs.text:
These only run when you explicitly trigger them from the paper detail page:

Action Endpoint What it does Regenerate summary POST /{id}/regenerate-summary Re-runs Claude summary on stored raw_text Re-extract abstract POST /{id}/reextract-abstract Regex + Claude Haiku on raw_text Re-extract references GET /{id}/ai-extract-references Forces Claude Haiku reference extraction Extract figures triggered from Figures tab Re-runs Docling / pypdf pipeline

docs.title: First steps
docs.text:
This page takes one paper from upload to concept map. It assumes PaperManager is already running and you can log in; if not, start with Hosting your own.

Plan about ten minutes, most of it waiting for the AI steps to finish in the background.

docs.title: 1. Add a paper
docs.text:
1. Open Library (the first item in the top menu).
  2. Click + (Add paper). Drag a PDF into the drop zone, or paste a link such as https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.00364.
  3. PaperManager looks up title, authors, year and DOI on Semantic Scholar and CrossRef. A badge shows where the details came from; yellow or red means please check.
  4. Fix anything that is wrong and confirm.

The paper appears in your library straight away. Summary, topics, figures and references are added in the background over the next minute or two.

Many papers at once

Drop several PDFs at once, or click + → Import multiple papers at once and paste a list of DOIs, arXiv IDs or URLs. See Ingesting papers.

docs.title: 2. Open it and read
docs.text:
Click the paper. The view has two halves:

Left side Right side PDF, abstract, summary, figures, tables, references, related papers, claims Notes, Chat, Highlights, Concepts, Tour

Try these in order:

  • Summary (left): the AI summary of the whole paper.
  • Figures (left): every figure with its caption; ask a question about one.
  • Chat (right): ask anything about this paper, e.g. "What is the main limitation?"
  • Highlights: select text in the PDF to highlight it in a colour; highlights are listed here.

docs.title: 3. Let it explain the paper
docs.text:
Two tabs on the right help with hard papers. Both are explained in Concepts, tour and concept map.

  • Tour → Make a quick tour. You get an overview, a list of sections you can skip, and 6–12 stops. Click a stop (or use ← / →) and the PDF jumps to the passage it is about.
  • Concepts → Find concepts. PaperManager marks ideas on the PDF pages that a picture explains better than text, and draws an animation, plot or formula breakdown for each one.

docs.title: 4. Put it in a project
docs.text:
1. Open Projects, type a name and click Create.
  2. In the project, use Search library to add a paper… to add your paper (and a few more).
  3. Click Concept map. Each paper's key concepts are extracted and joined into one graph. Concepts shared by several papers grow larger; the filters narrow it by author, year or kind of concept.

docs.title: 5. Ask across everything
docs.text:
Open Knowledge in the top menu and ask a question, for example:

@project:MyThesis Which papers compare against diffusion baselines, and how do they differ?

The answer cites the papers it used. Leave out the @project: part to search the whole library, or turn on web search for questions your papers do not cover. More in Knowledge features.

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Library: search, filters and views
  • Reading a paper: every tab of the paper view
  • MCP server: use your library from Claude Desktop or Claude Code

docs.title: Local development
docs.text: This page sets PaperManager up from source, with the backend and frontend running directly on your machine so code changes show up immediately. To simply use PaperManager, the Docker setup in Hosting your own is quicker.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Requirement Version Notes Python 3.11+ Use conda or pyenv Node.js 18+ For the frontend Neo4j 5.x Local Docker container (below) or a free AuraDB instance Google account — Google Drive for PDF storage Anthropic API key — Claude for summaries & chat Ollama (optional) latest Local AI for metadata extraction

docs.title: 1 — Clone the repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/NiklasAbraham/PaperManager
cd PaperManager

docs.title: 2 — Set up the Python environment
docs.text:
conda create -n papermanager python=3.11 -y
conda activate papermanager
pip install -r backend/requirements.txt

docs.title: 3 — Install the frontend
docs.text:
cd frontend
npm install
cd ..

docs.title: 4 — Install Ollama (optional, recommended)
docs.text:
Ollama is used for local metadata extraction (layer 2), tag suggestions, Cypher assist, and figure captions. Without it the system still works using Semantic Scholar and Claude.

# macOS
brew install ollama

# Linux
curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh

# Pull the model
ollama pull llama3.2:3b

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Copy the example environment file and fill in your credentials:

cp .env.example .env

Edit .env:

# ── Neo4j ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
NEO4J_URI=bolt://localhost:7687
NEO4J_USER=neo4j
NEO4J_PASSWORD=your-password

# ── Google Drive ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# OAuth desktop app credentials from Google Cloud Console
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=xxxx.apps.googleusercontent.com
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=xxxx
GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID=xxxx   # Folder where PDFs will be stored

# ── Anthropic ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-xxxx

# Anthropic Foundry enterprise gateway (optional)
ANTHROPIC_WORK_API_KEY=xxxx
ANTHROPIC_WORK_BASE_URL=https://your-foundry-gateway.com/...

# ── App ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BACKEND_PORT=8000
FRONTEND_URL=http://localhost:5173

# ── Ollama ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
OLLAMA_MODEL=llama3.2:3b

# ── Corporate network (optional) ──────────────────────────────
SSL_VERIFY=true
SSL_CA_BUNDLE=/path/to/corporate-ca.pem

docs.title: Neo4j setup
docs.text:
The quickest option is a local container:

docker run -d --name papermanager-neo4j -p 7687:7687 -p 7474:7474 \
  -e NEO4J_AUTH=neo4j/change-me neo4j:5

Then set NEO4J_URI=bolt://localhost:7687, NEO4J_USER=neo4j and NEO4J_PASSWORD=change-me in .env. A free AuraDB instance works too: copy its neo4j+s:// URI and credentials instead.

docs.title: Google Drive setup
docs.text:
1. Go to Google Cloud Console
  2. Create a project and enable the Google Drive API
  3. Create OAuth 2.0 credentials (Desktop application type)
  4. Download the credentials JSON
  5. On first backend start, a browser window opens for OAuth authorisation
  6. Credentials are saved to backend/token.json and reused automatically

docs.title: Starting the Application
docs.text:
./start.sh

This script:

  • Starts the FastAPI backend on port 8000 (logs → /tmp/papermanager-backend.log)
  • Starts the Vite frontend on port 5173 (logs → /tmp/papermanager-frontend.log)
  • Optionally starts Ollama if configured

Open http://localhost:5173 in your browser.

Checking logs

tail -f /tmp/papermanager-backend.log
tail -f /tmp/papermanager-frontend.log

docs.title: First Run
docs.text:
On startup the backend automatically:

  1. Verifies the Neo4j connection
  2. Runs schema setup (creates indexes and constraints)
  3. Seeds 157 default tags across source, workflow, content, and domain categories

You should see the library page with a drop zone and a + button to add papers.

docs.title: What's Next?
docs.text:
• First steps — one paper from upload to concept map
  • Ingest your first paper — drag a PDF or paste a URL
  • Browse the library — search, filter, sort your papers
  • Chat with a paper — ask Claude questions about any paper
  • Explore the knowledge graph — visualise connections

docs.title: Ingesting Papers
docs.text: PaperManager supports three ways to add papers to your library.

docs.title: PDF Upload
docs.text: Drag a PDF onto the Library page or click the + button → PDF tab.

docs.title: What Happens Automatically
docs.text:
The upload follows a multi-step pipeline:

flowchart TD
    A[📄 PDF uploaded] --> B[Extract text with Docling]
    B --> C{DOI / arXiv ID\nin text?}
    C -->|Yes| D[Semantic Scholar API]
    D -->|Not found| E[CrossRef API]
    C -->|No title found| F[Ollama LLM on first 3 000 chars]
    F -->|Ollama unavailable| G[Regex heuristics]
    D --> H[Confirmation modal]
    E --> H
    F --> H
    G --> H
    H -->|User confirms| I[Upload PDF to Google Drive]
    I --> J[Create Paper node in Neo4j]
    J --> K[Generate AI summary — Claude Opus]
    K --> L[Suggest topics — Claude Haiku]
    L --> M[Extract references]
    M --> N[Extract figures from PDF]
    N --> O[✅ Paper ready in library]

docs.title: Step-by-Step: The Upload Modal
docs.text:
After choosing a PDF you walk through up to five optional steps (each can be toggled in Settings):

  1. Metadata confirmation — review extracted title, year, authors, DOI, venue; fix any errors
  2. Source — record how you found this paper (person, LinkedIn, Twitter, conference, newsletter…)
  3. Summary prompt — edit the Claude prompt before the AI summary is generated
  4. References review — approve which references to save as CITES links
  5. Tags — review AI-suggested tags before saving

docs.title: Upload Modal Options
docs.text: Option Default Description Source step on Record how you found the paper Summary prompt step on Edit the AI summary instructions Auto-save references off Skip review and save all references automatically Tags step on Review AI-suggested tags before saving

docs.title: Metadata Source Badge
docs.text:
After upload each paper card shows a colour-coded badge:

Colour Source 🟢 Green Semantic Scholar or CrossRef 🟡 Yellow Ollama LLM extraction 🔴 Red Heuristic guess

docs.title: URL / DOI Ingest
docs.text:
Click + → URL / DOI tab. Paste any of:

Input format Example arXiv URL https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762 arXiv ID 1706.03762 or arXiv:1706.03762 DOI URL https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14539 Bare DOI 10.1038/nature14539 PubMed URL https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12345678/ bioRxiv URL https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/... medRxiv URL https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.1101/...

docs.title: What Happens
docs.text:
1. The URL/ID is parsed to detect the source type
  2. Metadata is fetched from the appropriate API (arXiv Atom, Semantic Scholar, CrossRef, PubMed eUtils, bioRxiv)
  3. If a DOI is found, Semantic Scholar is queried for richer data (citation count, affiliations, topics)
  4. Paper is auto-tagged from-url
  5. No PDF is stored — the paper is metadata-only

Note

To get a PDF for a URL-ingested paper, open the Paper Detail page and click Upload PDF.

docs.title: Bulk Import
docs.text:
Go to Bulk Import in the nav bar. Upload or paste a JSON file:

{
  "fetch_pdf": true,
  "project_id": "optional-project-uuid",
  "papers": [
    {"url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762"},
    {"arxiv": "1810.04805"},
    {"doi": "10.1038/nature14539"},
    {"url": "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30082513/"},
    {"title": "AlphaFold protein structure prediction"},
    {"title": "CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing", "fetch_pdf": false}
  ]
}

Each entry needs at least one of: url, arxiv, doi, title. Formats can be mixed freely.

A sample file is included at sample_bulk_import.json.

docs.title: Resolution Order
docs.text:
For each paper entry the system tries, in order:

flowchart LR
    E1["url → URL resolver"] --> E2["arxiv → arXiv API"]
    E2 --> E3["doi → S2 → CrossRef"]
    E3 --> E4["title → S2 title search\n→ arXiv title search\n→ Ollama-improved arXiv"]

docs.title: PDF Fetching
docs.text:
When fetch_pdf: true:

  • arXiv papers — downloaded from arxiv.org/pdf/{id}
  • Other papers — Unpaywall API checked for an open-access PDF URL

docs.title: Progress Stream
docs.text:
Bulk import shows a live log stream as papers are processed. Papers that already exist by DOI are reported as "skipped". All imported papers are auto-tagged bulk-import.

Project assignment

Set "project_id" in the JSON to automatically add all imported papers to a project.

docs.title: Duplicate Detection
docs.text:
Before a paper is saved, a duplicate check runs against existing papers:

  • Exact DOI match → blocked (the paper already exists)
  • High title similarity → warning shown in the confirmation modal

If a DOI-matched stub already exists (from reference extraction), the stub is enriched with full metadata rather than creating a duplicate.

docs.title: Knowledge Features
docs.text: PaperManager includes three advanced knowledge tools: an interactive graph, a multi-paper AI chat, and a direct Cypher query editor.

docs.title: Knowledge Graph
docs.text: Navigate to Graph in the nav bar for an interactive WebGL visualisation of your entire library.

docs.title: Node Types
docs.text: Colour Node type 🟣 Purple Paper 🔵 Blue Person 🟢 Green Topic 🟠 Orange Tag 🩷 Pink Project ⚫ Grey Note

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
• Pan — click and drag the background
  • Zoom — scroll or pinch
  • Move nodes — drag individual nodes
  • Click a node — opens a properties panel on the right:
  • View all node properties
  • Navigate to the paper detail page
  • Delete the node

docs.title: Graph Modes
docs.text:
Mode What is shown Full graph All node types (up to 500 nodes) Papers only Papers, People, Topics Single paper One paper with all its direct neighbours

Switch modes using the toggle in the top-left of the graph.

docs.title: Display Options
docs.text:
Use the sliders and toggles in the control panel to adjust:

  • Node size
  • Link distance
  • Repulsion force
  • Show / hide node labels
  • Show / hide edge labels

docs.title: Knowledge Chat
docs.text: Navigate to Knowledge in the nav bar to chat with Claude about multiple papers at once.

docs.title: Conversation
docs.text:
Type a question. By default the 10 most recently added papers are used as context.

Use @mentions to bring specific papers or groups into context:

Mention syntax What is loaded @paper:Attention is All You Need That specific paper @tag:deep-learning All papers with that tag @topic:Protein Folding All papers about that topic @project:my-phd-papers All papers in that project

docs.title: Example Prompts
docs.text:
@tag:deep-learning What are the main architectural differences across these papers?

@topic:Protein Folding How has the approach changed from RoseTTAFold to AlphaFold?

@project:my-phd-papers Summarise the key open problems.

@paper:Attention is All You Need What positional encoding does this use?

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Feature Description SSE streaming Answer appears token by token Step-by-step progress Shows which Cypher queries fetch context, how many papers are loaded Context visualisation Stacked bar chart of token usage per paper Model selector Claude Opus, Claude Work (enterprise), Ollama Conversation history Create new conversations, load previous ones Compact Summarise conversation history into a system message to free up context

docs.title: Context Assembly
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Q["User question"] --> P["Parse @mentions"]
    P -->|"Mentions found"| C["Cypher queries to fetch\nmatching papers"]
    P -->|"No mentions"| R["10 most recently added papers"]
    C --> A["Assemble context\n(truncated to token budget per paper)"]
    R --> A
    A --> S["Stream Claude Opus response via SSE"]

docs.title: Cypher Editor
docs.text: Navigate to Cypher in the nav bar for direct access to the Neo4j database.

docs.title: Schema Browser
docs.text:
A live view of all:

  • Node labels and their property keys
  • Relationship types
  • Fulltext indexes

docs.title: Query Editor
docs.text: Write and run raw Cypher queries. Results are shown in a table. Mutation counters show nodes created/deleted, relationships created/deleted, and properties set. Maximum 500 rows are returned.

docs.title: AI Assist
docs.text: Describe what you want in plain English — Ollama generates the Cypher query for you. You can then review and run it.

docs.title: Example Queries
docs.text:
-- Papers citing a specific paper
MATCH (a:Paper)-[:CITES]->(b:Paper {title: "..."})
RETURN a.title, a.year

-- Most connected authors
MATCH (p:Person)<-[:AUTHORED_BY]-(paper:Paper)
RETURN p.name, count(paper) AS papers ORDER BY papers DESC LIMIT 10

-- Papers without summaries
MATCH (p:Paper) WHERE p.summary IS NULL RETURN p.title, p.year

-- All papers on a topic
MATCH (p:Paper)-[:ABOUT]->(t:Topic {name: "Transformers"})
RETURN p.title, p.year ORDER BY p.year DESC

-- Papers shared by a colleague
MATCH (person:Person {name: "Jan"})<-[:INVOLVES {role: "shared_by"}]-(p:Paper)
RETURN p.title, p.year

docs.title: People
docs.text:
Navigate to People in the nav bar.

All people in the system are listed in the sidebar with search.

Person detail shows:

  • Name and affiliation
  • Papers where they are an author (AUTHORED_BY)
  • Papers where they have an INVOLVES role (shared_by, working_on, collaborating, etc.)
  • Research specialties (linked Topic nodes via SPECIALIZES)

People are auto-created when papers are ingested from the author list.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
Navigate to Projects in the nav bar.

Create named collections of papers:

  • Create a project with name, description, and status (active / paused / done)
  • Add/remove papers from a project
  • Papers can belong to multiple projects
  • Filter the library by project
  • Link projects as related (RELATED_TO)
  • Select a project during upload, URL ingest, or bulk import to add papers automatically

docs.title: Export
docs.text: Format How BibTeX GET /export/bibtex — downloads a .bib file containing all papers JSON Available from the Settings page

docs.title: Backfill (Bulk Enrichment)
docs.text:
Run from the Settings page or directly via the API:

Operation Endpoint Description Backfill topics POST /backfill/topics Run Claude Haiku topic suggestion on all papers without topics Backfill summaries POST /backfill/summary Generate AI summaries for papers that have raw_text but no summary Backfill figures POST /backfill/figures Extract figures from all papers that have a PDF but no figures yet

Each returns {processed, skipped, errors}.

docs.title: Library
docs.text: The Library is the main page of PaperManager (/). It shows all papers in your collection and provides powerful search and filtering tools.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
When no filters are active you see a dashboard at the top showing:

  • Count cards — total papers, authors, topics, tags, projects
  • Papers by year bar chart
  • Top topics list
  • Recently added papers

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
The search bar at the top performs full-text search across:

  • Paper title
  • Abstract
  • AI-generated summary

Results update as you type. The search query is reflected in the URL so you can bookmark filtered views.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The left sidebar provides filters that narrow down the paper list:

Filter How it works Tag Shows papers tagged with the selected tag Topic Shows papers about the selected research topic Project Shows papers belonging to the selected project Person Shows papers authored by or involving the selected person

Multiple filters can be combined. Active filters appear as removable chips below the search bar.

docs.title: View mode
docs.text:
Toggle between grid and list view using the buttons in the top-right corner.

  • Grid — compact cards ideal for large libraries
  • List — more detail per row, easier to scan metadata

docs.title: Sort
docs.text: Sort option Description Date added ↓ Newest first (default) Date added ↑ Oldest first Year ↓ Latest publication year first Title A→Z Alphabetical

docs.title: Page size
docs.text: Choose how many papers to show per page: 20, 50, 100, or All.

docs.title: Paper Cards
docs.text:
Each paper card shows:

  • Title and year
  • Authors (up to 3, then "et al.")
  • Metadata source badge (colour-coded: green / yellow / red)
  • Abstract preview (toggleable in Settings)
  • Tags as coloured pills
  • Quick edit and delete buttons

Click any card to open the Paper Detail view.

docs.title: Adding Papers
docs.text:
From the Library page:

  • Drag and drop a PDF file onto the page → upload flow starts
  • Click the + button → choose PDF upload or URL/DOI ingest
  • Navigate to Bulk Import in the nav bar for batch import

docs.title: Settings Reference
docs.text:
Library display settings are persisted to localStorage:

Setting Options Default Default view grid / list grid Default sort date desc/asc, year desc, title asc date desc Abstract preview on / off on Papers per page 20 / 50 / 100 / all 20

See Settings for all available options.

docs.title: MCP Server (Claude Desktop)
docs.text: PaperManager ships with an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server at backend/mcp_server.py. This lets Claude Desktop interact with your library directly via natural language.

docs.title: 1 — Locate your Python binary
docs.text:
conda activate papermanager
which python
# e.g. /Users/you/miniconda3/envs/papermanager/bin/python

docs.title: 2 — Configure Claude Desktop
docs.text:
Edit ~/.claude/claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "paperManager": {
      "command": "/path/to/conda/envs/papermanager/bin/python",
      "args": ["/path/to/PaperManager/backend/mcp_server.py"]
    }
  }
}

Replace the paths with your actual paths. Restart Claude Desktop.

docs.title: 3 — Verify
docs.text: Ask Claude: "Can you list my recent papers?" — Claude should call search_papers and return results from your library.

docs.title: Available Tools
docs.text: Tool Description search_papers Search by keyword, tag, topic, project, or person get_paper_detail Full paper metadata for one paper chat_with_paper Ask a question about a paper's content add_note Write or update a paper's markdown note get_note Read a paper's note tag_paper_with Add a tag to a paper add_topic Link a research topic to a paper link_person_to_paper Link a person to a paper with a role add_paper_metadata Add a paper by metadata only (no PDF) list_projects List all projects list_project_papers Papers in a specific project add_to_project Add a paper to a project list_tags All tags with paper counts list_topics All topics with paper counts list_people All people get_person_papers Papers associated with a person add_person Create a person node create_project Create a new project upload_pdf Add a paper with its PDF (local path, URL, arXiv id or DOI) find_duplicates Duplicate groups, each with the paper to keep merge_papers Merge duplicates into one paper, nothing lost (dry_run by default) update_paper_metadata Correct title, year, venue, DOI, abstract or the author list regenerate_summary Re-run the AI summary from the stored full text delete_paper Delete a paper with its note, highlights and PDF (needs confirm=true)

docs.title: Example Interactions
docs.text:
You: add a note to the Attention is All You Need paper saying
     "@Jan is working on a follow-up to this approach"

Claude: [calls add_note] → note saved, MENTIONS relationship
        created in Neo4j for Jan

You: what papers do I have tagged "to-read" about protein folding?

Claude: [calls search_papers with tag="to-read", topic="Protein Folding"]
        → returns matching papers

You: create a project called "NeurIPS 2025 prep" and add all papers
     tagged "important" to it

Claude: [calls create_project, then search_papers + add_to_project
        for each paper]

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The MCP server and FastAPI backend share the same service and database layers:

flowchart LR
    CD["Claude Desktop"] -->|"MCP protocol"| MCP["mcp_server.py"]
    Browser["Browser"] -->|"HTTP"| FastAPI["FastAPI routers/"]
    MCP --> Tools["tools/*.py"]
    FastAPI --> Routers["routers/*.py"]
    Tools --> DB["db/queries/"]
    Routers --> DB
    Tools --> Services["services/"]
    Routers --> Services
    DB --> Neo4j["Neo4j Aura"]
    Services --> Drive["Google Drive"]
    Services --> AI["Claude / Ollama"]

PDF upload via MCP

upload_pdf(source, project) runs one paper through the full upload pipeline. source is a local PDF path, a PDF URL, an arXiv id or a DOI. Local paths must lie under HOST_IMPORT_ROOT (e.g. /srv/papers), which is mounted read-only into the backend container.

docs.title: Running the MCP Server Standalone
docs.text:
The server can also be run without Claude Desktop for testing:

conda activate papermanager
cd /path/to/PaperManager
python backend/mcp_server.py

This starts the MCP server in stdio mode, ready to accept tool calls.

docs.title: Paper Detail
docs.text: Click any paper card to open the Paper Detail view (/paper/:id). It has four main panels.

docs.title: Metadata & Abstract
docs.text:
The left panel shows:

  • Title, year, DOI, venue
  • Citation count (from Semantic Scholar)
  • Metadata source badge
  • Authors — click an author chip to open their People profile
  • Topics — click a topic chip to filter the library to that topic
  • Abstract (original)
  • AI summary (generated by Claude Opus during upload)

Click Edit to open a modal where you can update any field.

docs.title: PDF Viewer
docs.text:
Available when a PDF was uploaded (not for URL-only papers). The PDF is streamed from Google Drive and rendered inline in the browser.

Tip

For URL-ingested papers you can still attach a PDF later via the Upload PDF button in the metadata panel.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
Figures are extracted from the PDF and stored on Google Drive. The figures panel shows:

  • Figure number and page number
  • Caption (generated by Docling, Ollama, or Claude Vision)
  • Click any figure for full-size view
  • Ask about this figure — opens a vision chat powered by Claude; ask anything about the figure image

docs.title: Extracting Figures
docs.text:
Click Extract Figures and choose a caption method:

Method Description Docling Structural PDF parser — fast, no AI cost Ollama Local LLM captions (default) Claude Vision Highest quality; uses Anthropic API

The default method can be set in Settings.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text: A Markdown editor is attached to each paper.

docs.title: Special Syntax
docs.text:
Syntax Effect @PersonName Links to a Person node; creates it if not found #TopicName Links to a Topic node; creates it if not found

When you save a note, all @mentions and #topics become graph relationships:

(Note)-[:MENTIONS]->(Person)
(Note)-[:MENTIONS]->(Topic)

This means you can later query "all notes that mention @Jan" or "all papers with notes about #transformers" from the Cypher editor or knowledge chat.

docs.title: Preview
docs.text: Toggle Preview mode to render the note as formatted Markdown.

docs.title: Chat with Paper
docs.text: Ask natural language questions about the paper's full text. The raw_text extracted from the PDF is included in the context (truncated to model limits).

docs.title: Model Options
docs.text: Model Provider Best for Claude Opus 4.6 Anthropic (personal key) Highest quality answers Claude Work Anthropic Foundry gateway Enterprise environments Ollama (llama3.2:3b) Local Fully offline

docs.title: Example Questions
docs.text:
What is the main contribution of this paper?
How does this method compare to previous approaches?
What are the key limitations mentioned by the authors?
Can you explain the loss function used in equation 3?

docs.title: Outgoing References
docs.text:
Papers that this paper cites. Extracted on-demand and shown in a review list before being saved.

Extraction pipeline (tries in order):

  1. Semantic Scholar /references API (requires DOI)
  2. Regex on the REFERENCES section of raw_text
  3. Claude Haiku on the last 30% of the document (when earlier strategies return < 3 results)

Each saved reference creates a Paper stub node (title + DOI), tagged from-references, and linked with a CITES relationship. If you later import the full paper by DOI, the stub is enriched rather than duplicated.

docs.title: Incoming Citations
docs.text: Papers in your library that cite this paper. Maintained automatically as you import papers.

docs.title: Concepts, tour and concept map
docs.text:
Three tools help you understand papers rather than just store them. Concepts and the Tour work on one paper; the concept map works on a whole project.

Tool Where What you get Needs Concepts Paper view → Concepts tab Visual explanations of ideas, marked on the PDF page Claude (subscription or API key) Tour Paper view → Tour tab An overview and 6–12 stops through the PDF Claude Code on a subscription Concept map Projects → a project → Concept map One graph of the key concepts across all papers in the project An OpenAI-compatible model (LITELLM_*)

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text:
1. Open a paper with a PDF and switch to the Concepts tab.
  2. Click Find concepts. The pages are read in batches; on each page, up to three ideas that a picture explains best are marked.
  3. Click a concept to generate its visualisation, or Generate all for the rest.

Each concept gets one of four kinds of visualisation:

  • Formula: an equation broken into its parts, with what each symbol means
  • Graph: a plot drawn from data points (lines, points or bars)
  • Explanation: a short structured text
  • Animation: a small 2D animation, run in a sandboxed frame

Clicking a mark on the PDF opens its concept, and the other way round. This feature is adapted from Get It. (Apache-2.0).

docs.title: Quick tour
docs.text:
Open the Tour tab and click Make a quick tour. After a minute you get:

  • an overview of what the paper does and why it matters,
  • what to skip on a first read,
  • 6–12 stops, each tied to an exact passage in the PDF, with a short explanation and the concepts it relies on.

Click a stop, or press ← / →, and the PDF scrolls to that passage and highlights it. The tour is saved with the paper; Regenerate tour makes a new one.

Setup

The tour runs Sonnet through Claude Code on a Claude subscription. Set CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (from claude setup-token) and CLAUDE_CODE_USERS in .env. Without them the button stays disabled; there is no API-key fallback.

docs.title: Concept map
docs.text:
The concept map shows what a set of papers is about and how the ideas connect.

  • Circles are concepts; the colour is the kind (method, model, dataset, task, …) and the size is how many papers discuss it.
  • Papers can be shown too, sized by citations, with their authors optional.
  • Lines are typed relations from the papers: is a, part of, uses, extends, improves on, alternative to, evaluated on and more.
  • Filters narrow the map by author, year, kind and the minimum number of papers per concept. The list beside the graph groups all concepts by kind.

Papers are mapped automatically: every ten minutes, PaperManager maps project papers that have a summary but no concepts yet. Map new papers does it right away; Rebuild all starts over. Set CONCEPT_MAP_AUTO=false to switch the automatic run off.

For each paper the model returns 6–15 concepts with the paper's role for each (introduces, extends, uses, evaluates, critiques or background). It reuses names that already exist in the project, so the same idea from two papers becomes one circle.
